Raw predicates, ranges, mutations, ordering, and cursor positions compare exact bytes; VARCHAR uses strict prefix or explicit fixed-host normalization.
A bounded streaming visitor rejects signed Db2 catalogs at table/nested/text/aggregate/duplicate limits before full graph allocation or provider mutation.
Every top-level package section count is checked in the first allocation-free aggregate preflight.
Round-one, round-two, work-package, and round-three evidence discover unique trailer-bound commits and validate Git object bytes with canonical PathBuf ordering.
Db2 in-place compatibility covers every normalized semantic field; DDL preserves only the non-SQL extract projection after full SQL equality.
Retained packages and selection are durable and signature-revalidated; one identity-bound publication state machine recovers explicit partial controller/Db2 states.
Production package trust stores SecretRef values, resolves non-cloneable zeroizing secrets per verification, and exposes no signing operation.
